newsitem.title: USA: NYSE bars three individuals for rules violations.
newsitem.headline: NYSE bars three individuals for rules violations.

text.p: The New York Stock Exchange said on Wednesday it permanently barred three individuals from exchange-related business for violating federal securities law or exchange rules.

In one case, the NYSE permanently barred Alan Burton of Brooklyn, N.Y., a former employee in the cashier's department at member firm Wagner Stott Clearing Corp, after Burton pled guilty in court to improperly redirecting about $1 million in firm funds to bank accounts under his control.

The NYSE said it also imposed a permanent bar against John Goldsmith of Long Beach, N.Y. after a hearing panel found the former D.H. Blair & Co Inc broker had arranged with the help of a clerk to receive about $325,000 in inflated commissions. Goldsmith did not respond to the charges, the exchange said.
The NYSE permanently barred former specialist Robert Mosca of Malverne, N.Y. for failing to comply with an NYSE inquiry.

The exchange also suspended for six weeks Gregory Fabio of Pleasantville, N.Y. Fabio, who formerly worked at Prudential Securities, was charged with improperly trading for an account more than six months after the death of the account holder.
